lines.en: What a society argues about in public tells you what it values in private.
It is easier to win an election with a slogan than to govern with one.
Were voting alone enough to build a democracy, the world would be full of them.
However unpopular a truth may be, a healthy society must make room for it to be said.
Not until citizens can criticize power without fear is freedom of speech more than a decoration.
The measure of a politician, it is said, is not how they treat their supporters, but how they treat their opponents.
What the crowd demands today, it may punish tomorrow; that is why leadership means more than listening.
The proposal was popular, persuasive, and, on closer inspection, completely unaffordable.
Little is more dangerous to public life than the moment when loyalty replaces honesty.
Rarely does power give up its privileges voluntarily; every right we have was argued for, at length.
What the constitution promises on paper, the courts must defend in practice, or the paper means nothing.
It is the quiet work of compromise, never applauded, that keeps a public life functioning.
Were every promise costed before it was made, election campaigns would be silent affairs.
Not until a law applies equally to those who wrote it does it deserve the name of justice.
However loud the politics becomes, the citizen's daily question remains simple: is my life better this year?
